**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-09**
**Reference number:** POC-8E86334152-82903
**Member:** Skyler Ellison — **Member ID:** W656322877
**Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
**Governing policy:** Premera Blue Cross Medical Policy, *Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590)*, effective April 1, 2026 — https://www.premera.com/medicalpolicies/7.01.590.pdf

---

Dear Member Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which Premera denied in the notice dated August 9, 2026. The stated reason for the denial was that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking Premera to reconsider that decision, because the imaging in my chart matches the findings the plan's own policy lists, and my surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this surgery is needed.

Below I set out Premera's own criteria from *Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590)* and point to where each one appears in the records that were submitted.

## The plan's criteria and the records

**1. Diagnosis.** The policy states:

> "There is a documented diagnosis of one of the following: o Degenerative joint disease (DJD) o Osteoarthritis (OA) o Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) o Traumatic arthritis o Avascular necrosis"

My chart records a qualifying diagnosis: [diagnosis exactly as written by Dr. Reyes, and the date of that note]. The supporting findings are described below.

**2. Need for treatment.** The policy states:

> "Treatment is needed because of one or more of the following: o Disabling pain for at least 3 months duration o Functional disability which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living for at least 3 months duration"

and

> "For a total shoulder arthroplasty and degenerative joint disease such as osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis or traumatic arthritis or osteonecrosis ALL of the following are present: o Needs treatment because of disabling pain and/or limited shoulder function interfering with activities of daily living (ADLs)"

My records document 14 months of progressive pain in the shoulder that is not relieved by rest. They also document that I cannot reach overhead, cannot dress without help, and cannot sleep on the affected side. On examination, my active forward elevation is limited to 90 degrees and external rotation to 10 degrees, with glenohumeral crepitus and intact cuff strength. The duration is more than four times the three months the policy describes, and the limitations listed are basic activities of daily living.

**3. Imaging — the reason given for the denial.** This is the criterion the denial turns on, and it is the one the records meet most directly. The policy states:

> "Radiographic or imaging evidence (e.g., X-ray, CT, MRI) of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by ONE or more of the following: o Irregular joint surfaces o Glenoid sclerosis o Glenoid osteophyte changes o Flattened glenoid o Cystic changes in the humeral head o Joint space narrowing"

and, in the same terms:

> "Imaging evidence of destructive degenerative joint disease of the shoulder in the 12 months prior to surgery as evidenced by one or more of the following: irregular joint surfaces, glenoid sclerosis, glenoid osteophyte changes, flattened glenoid, cystic changes in the humeral head or joint space narrowing"

My shoulder radiographs (true AP and axillary) dated **May 27, 2026** report **complete loss of glenohumeral joint space, osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid**. A CT confirms an intact rotator cuff.

The policy asks for **one or more** of the listed findings. My imaging documents several of them: joint space narrowing (here, complete loss of joint space), glenoid osteophyte changes, sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. The study is dated May 27, 2026, well within the twelve-month window the policy describes relative to my planned surgery date of [planned surgery date, if scheduled]. On the face of the plan's own list, this criterion is met, and I would ask the reviewer to compare the radiology report directly against the six findings quoted above.

**4. Conservative medication management.** The policy states:

> "Documentation of three months of failed non-operative conservative management as demonstrated by a trial of one or more of the following: o Anti-inflammatory medications or analgesics o Intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate"

My records document NSAIDs for **six months** with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on **May 22, 2026** that gave only about two weeks of partial relief. That is both of the listed options, over a period twice as long as the three months described.

**5. Supervised physical measures.** The policy states:

> "A 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: o Physical therapy"

I completed supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening — **10 weeks, from May 5, 2026 to July 14, 2026, 20 visits**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. That exceeds the six-week trial the policy describes and was directed by a healthcare professional.

The policy also combines these last two requirements:

> "History of unsuccessful three-month trial of failed non-operative conservative management of one or more of the following medications: anti-inflammatory drugs or analgesics, or intra-articular injection of corticosteroids as appropriate, and a 6 week trial of one or more of the following physical measures under the direction of a healthcare professional: physical therapy, or flexibility and muscle strengthening exercises, or reasonable restriction of activities."

Both halves of that sentence are documented in my chart.

**6. Other pathways.** The policy separately provides that:

> "Total shoulder arthroplasty may be considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions: • Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union • Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue • Failed hemi-arthroplasty • Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction"

and that:

> "For other conditions, detailed clinical documentation supporting the diagnosis of one of the following: o Proximal humerus fracture malunion or non-union o Reconstruction after tumor resection of the glenohumeral joint or surrounding tissue o Failed hemi-arthroplasty o Post-traumatic injury (e.g., fracture, infection) causing shoulder joint destruction"

My request does not rest on those alternate pathways; it rests on the degenerative-disease criteria quoted above.

Finally, the policy states:

> "The individual’s medical records submitted for review for all conditions should document that medical necessity criteria are met for the procedure requested."

I believe the records do exactly that, and I am resubmitting them with this appeal.

## One request for clarity

Some of the criteria I have quoted introduce lists of further conditions that were not reproduced in the excerpts available to me, so there may be additional requirements in *Shoulder Arthroplasty (7.01.590)* that I have not addressed here. I have quoted only language I can verify as the plan's own; I have not paraphrased or reconstructed any policy text. If Premera relied on a specific criterion or threshold in this policy that my imaging was found not to meet, I ask that the reconsideration decision identify that criterion by name and explain which finding in the May 27, 2026 radiology report was considered insufficient, so that I and Dr. Reyes can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Premera to overturn the denial dated August 9, 2026 (reference POC-8E86334152-82903) and authorize the total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472, as requested by Dr. Reyes.

Enclosed with this letter are:

- [ ] A copy of the denial notice dated 2026-08-09
- [ ] Shoulder radiograph report dated 2026-05-27 and the CT report
- [ ] Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-05 to 2026-07-14, 20 visits)
- [ ] Office notes from Dr. Reyes, including medication history and the 2026-05-22 corticosteroid injection
- [ ] [Any other records you are enclosing]

I understand my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date I received notice of the decision, and that the notice states this appeal must be received by **February 5, 2027**. I am submitting it to Premera Blue Cross, Attn: Member Appeals, P.O. Box 91102, Seattle, WA 98111-9202, or by fax to 425-918-5592. (Members may also use Premera's Member Appeal form or call the number on their ID card.)

Thank you for taking a second look at this. Please contact me at the phone number above if anything further is needed, and please send the decision in writing.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Ellison**
